column1: # Reasons mentioning the 'definition sheet' refer to a draft withdrawn on 2026-10-19; the decisions were checked against CODEBOOK.md. Answers and reasons began as Claude pre-answers (claude_answer / claude_reason, 2026-10-19); the author reviewed them and kept all 40 unchanged.

column6: reason
L95 appends the unmatched line verbatim to out_lines with the [UNPARSED] prefix and continues; nothing is dropped. The write of out_lines to the file is outside the snippet.
column7: yes. An unparseable line is appended to out_lines as [UNPARSED - review this line] …, not dropped. The packet's extra snippet shows out_lines is written to the normalized file.

column6: L120-123 state the tie rule: archive entries first, then new entries in their original order. Per the definition sheet ("re-running changes nothing" = yes), the cited 3_merge_export.py:50-52 could support y; see report.
L184-196 build an entry with named counts (new_messages_added, duplicates_skipped, placeholders_superseded_by_archive) and json.dump it to LOG_PATH, a file.
L71-73: every messages row has source_uid, source_type and import_run_id. The file is reached through import_run_id (import run holds the source path, per the claim).
column7: yes. The messages table has NOT NULL source_uid, source_type and import_run_id columns, so every row records where it came from.

column6: L106-114 are the report block inside payload (closed at L115); L116 writes json.dumps(payload) to metadata_path.
L1043-1045 insert one (file_id, msg_hash) row per message hash the file contained.
column7: yes. INSERT OR IGNORE INTO file_messages (file_id, msg_hash) pairs each file with every message hash it contained.

column6: L343-345 declare redundant_count, unique_only_count and safe_to_delete per source_files row, stored in the SQLite DB.
L51: every Msg has source 'export'|'wts'|'msgstore'. This names the kind of import, not the file; two .txt exports both read 'export', so even partial is generous under the definition sheet.
L9 says "re-importing the same file must be a no-op". The definition sheet counts "re-running changes nothing" as yes, so this could be y rather than partial; see report.
L174 appends {type, importedAt, file, added, merged} to sources, L177 saves it, L178 returns it via res.json.
L201: SourceStoreIdentity, json source_store_identity. L197-198 say an empty value means unknown provenance, so it is not guaranteed to be filled.

L120-121 set conflicting[JID]=true when a second, different LID arrives. Detection only; no report is shown, which is the definition sheet's "silently keeps one version" case, so partial is open to challenge.
column7: Only marked in the code. The snippet sets an internal conflicting[c.JID] = true map flag and nothing is reported to the user. The "coded partial" claim says the same: the conflict is detected and resolved, with no report found. The snippet doesn't show anything past that map, so a report elsewhere in the code can't be ruled out.

column6: L93 says "exports deterministic JSONL shards". This is about the backup export, not the merged archive; partial matches the claim.
L52-54 insert source_rowid (message.SourceRowID) and observed_at for each event. Row id in the source DB, not the source file.
L30-32: on a differing handle it returns identityConflict naming existing service/id and new service/id. It is about handles (contacts), not message bodies; the definition says "message or item".

L122-123 say tombstones keep "deletion time, source, and reason"; L124-125 say edits and deletes are kept as "append-only revision events". README only; source is stated for tombstones, not every message.
L128 sets state = InProgress(Conflict{first_master_msg_id, first_slave_msg_id}). Per L122 and the claim, this only happens when sources carry ids, which the WhatsApp .txt loader does not.
L917-922 count matched messages whose columns differ, L923 stores the count in report.matched_message_diffs, L924-927 log.warn when n > 0.
L6: "write a validated RecordBatch (one txn, idempotent)". The same definition-sheet caveat applies as Q09: idempotence might count as y.
L559-563 print a before/after table and L565-571 one label with a right-aligned count per line. That out() goes to merge-report.txt (merge.py:597-598) is not in the snippet.

README L52 lists "Provenance + safe to purge advisor" as In progress, and L62 says "provenance: which backups/devices/paths". README only, unimplemented, per file not per message, so partial is the most it can be. The working-copy snippet is reformatted but readable.
L242-243: import_messages has import_id (references imports), message_id (references messages) and source_line, all NOT NULL.

L320 (read from the committed HEAD copy; the working copy is mangled) sets sourceId and sourceName on every message, plus lineIdx (a global, not per-file, counter). Under the definition sheet this could be y; see report.
L49: CREATE TABLE messages(... source_format INT ...). The format, not the file; the same caveat as Q08.
L306-307 assign a data_holder column per row: lookup by x.data_holder first, falling back to data_holders[x.file] (keyed by filepath, L303). It names whose export, not the file itself.
L65-66 state n_conversations exported files merged, orig_len messages before and merged_len after. A human-readable PDF/XLSX summary, so partial fits.
Both hits are the per-batch source_file in merge_log.json, which is the definition sheet's "only totals per file" case. The archive line format (2_normalize_export.py:110) has no source field.
All hits are sentiment vocabulary in the separate chat_analyzer tool; nothing in the merge code.

Whole files with nothing parsed are rejected (HTTP 400). A non-header line joins the previous message by the parser's continuation rule; that is parsing, not keeping unparseable input. No sign of retention.
0 grep hits. The merge rules (normalize.ts:4-10) combine the two sources without any disagreement output shown.
The CHANGELOG hit keeps message metadata when an attachment path is invalid; that is a bad field, not unparseable input. The narrow source search found 0 hits.

With --json, import prints ImportStats on stdout; the tool writes no summary file. Under the definition sheet (yes only if it writes a summary file; no if it only prints to the console) this is no. A borderline case; see Q40 and the report.
ndjson_parser.py:27 and :61: malformed lines are logged as warnings and skipped, the definition sheet's "no" example.
Hits are SQL ON CONFLICT upserts and verify.py count checks. The latest_merge_winner_source_counts in Q05 shows a winner is picked and counted, not that a disagreement is reported.
Deterministic applies only to generated ids (models.py:232, ARCHITECTURE.md:240); nothing states that the merged output is deterministic.
README.md:27 and app.py:1026: malformed elements are skipped with a log warning; lxml recover mode is parser repair, not retention.
app.py:499-503 drop the sender from the identity because sources disagree on it, which is silent handling. app.py:26 is about the cache.
Both hits are chart-zoom UI code in index.html.

Every message links to its import (import_id; the original archive is kept, :342-348) and to its source line. That is at least what sms_viewer (file_messages side table) and green2blue (import_run_id) got y for. Q22 yes plus Q39 yes do not conflict. :328-329 and :121 were not checked by me.
column7: yes. The import_messages insert runs in the loop over every parsed message. It stores import_id and source_line, and the parser sets source_line for each message. That is full per-record provenance, so it should be y, not partial.

column6: JSON on stdout only, behind an opt-in flag, with no file written, so it falls on the console side of the definition sheet. Yes is defensible only if "structured" means machine-readable rather than written to a file; if you take that reading, apply it to every tool.
column7: borderline, leaning no. The snippet only prints, as JSON with --json or as plain key=value lines without it. That is console output, and the packet's own WP3 convention says plain stdout lines don't count. A y needs evidence that ImportStats is returned or saved somewhere, which this snippet doesn't show.
